analysis.text:
Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 dated 2 February 1981, made by S. Silva, Licensed Surveyor, bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama, containing in extent 10 perches, by a final decree of a partition case bearing No. 111/P dated 2 February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama.

Gamini Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 March 1986, attested by R. Liyanage, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son, Suresh Perera, subject to the life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12 June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 dated 25 February 1991, attested by S. Sapumal, Notary Public.

Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children, namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5 June 2023, unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2 July 2022.

Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage, who is a citizen of the United States of America.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera up to the present owners in relation to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama. **(15 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(4 marks)**
3. Can Samantha become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera? Discuss with reference to the provisions of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, as amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018. **(2 marks)**
4. Explain the rules set out in sections 22 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. **(4 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

claims.text: The pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera cannot be fully established because the complete succession rules under the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 (specifically sections 23 to 26) are not provided in the retrieved text.

The shares presently owned by each heir in the property cannot be calculated because the available statutory evidence is incomplete and lacks key inheritance and distribution provisions for children and descendants under the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876.

Under Section 2(1) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, the transfer of title of any land in Sri Lanka to a foreigner is prohibited unless exempted. However, whether Samantha is barred from inheriting land through intestate succession cannot be determined because the full exemption provisions and the detailed terms of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018 are missing from the retrieved text.

Section 22 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 provides that when any person dies intestate leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person. The rules set out in sections 23 to 26 are missing from the retrieved text.

analysis.text:
Herath intends to mortgage his land situated in Anuradhapura, which is held under the Land Development Ordinance and is subject to the Land Development (Amendment) Act No. 11 of 2022, to a commercial bank in Sri Lanka for Rs. 10,000,000.

1. Calculate the stamp duty payable on the Mortgage Bond. Where should the stamp duty be paid? **(4 marks)**
2. Does Herath require approval from the Divisional Secretary to mortgage the land? **(4 marks)**
3. What are the instances in which the President of Sri Lanka could cancel a grant? Discuss with reference to the relevant provisions. **(4 marks)**
4. Herath passed away after the mortgage was settled and released in 2023. He failed to appoint a successor to the land. Who are the groups of relatives entitled to the land under the Third Schedule of the amended Land Development Ordinance? **(3 marks)**

**Total: 15 marks**

claims.text: Herath does not require approval from the Divisional Secretary to mortgage the land. Under Section 19(7) of the Land Development Ordinance, the approval of the Divisional Secretary is not required when mortgaging such a holding to a licensed commercial bank.

The specific instances in which the President of Sri Lanka could cancel a grant cannot be discussed because the substantive statutory provisions under Chapter VIII of the Land Development Ordinance are missing from the retrieved text, which only includes the chapter heading.

hits.excerpt: 48. (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed. (2) Where any property transferred for a consideration is subject to any mortgage, encumbrances or reservation of interest, stamp duty with which the instrument of transfer is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property transferred, without any deduction for the mortgage, encumbrances or reservation. (3) Where any property is gifted subject to any reservation in favour of the donor or any other person, stamp duty with which the instrument of gift is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if that property had been gifted to the donee without that reservation.

claims.text: Yes, Martin Perera can execute the Will and exclude his children without assigning any reason. Under Section 2(2) of the Wills Ordinance (as substituted by the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022), every testator has full power to make testamentary dispositions as they see fit, including the right to exclude, disinherit, or omit any child, parent, relative, or descendant without assigning any reason.

According to Section 2(1) of the Wills Ordinance (as substituted by the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022), the explicit statutory requirements are that the person executing the will must have reached eighteen years of age, may reside within or outside Sri Lanka, can dispose of property belonging to them at the time of death (which would otherwise devolve to heirs), and the beneficiary must not be legally incapacitated from receiving it. Additionally, Section 4 of the Wills Ordinance was repealed by Section 4 of the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022.

The provided statutory provisions do not specify the steps an executor must take after the death of a sole testator. The only procedural instruction provided states that upon the demise of a testator in a joint last will, testamentary proceedings must be instituted under Chapter XXXVIII or Chapter XXXVIIIB of the Civil Procedure Code to obtain probate or letters of administration with the will annexed.

The provided texts of the Notaries Ordinance, as amended, do not contain or specify any mandatory clause that a Notary must include in the attestation of a Last Will. The provisions only outline administrative duties, such as listing only the number and date of wills and codicils in the monthly list (and omitting executor names in the weekly list) delivered to the Registrar of Lands.

analysis.text:
By a Final Decree dated 5 May 2018, entered in partition case bearing No. 3535/P of the District Court of Nugegoda, Ajith Silva was allotted all that allotment of land marked Lot 2 depicted in Plan No. 1616 dated 2 March 2010, made by A. C. Perera, Licensed Surveyor, of the land called Kahatagahawatte, bearing Assessment No. 12, Temple Road, Nugegoda, containing in extent 15 perches.

Ajith Silva, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 December 2018, attested by P. C. Nonis, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot 2 depicted in Plan No. 1616 to Prabash Silva, the elder son of Ajith, subject to the life interest of the donor, and subject to the condition that Prabash shall not sell, mortgage or otherwise deal with the land, but may enjoy the produce thereof during his lifetime. On the death of Prabash, the property shall devolve free of all conditions to Subash, the younger son of Ajith Silva.

Ajith had three children, namely Prabash, Subash and Shehani, by his second marriage to Yamuna. Ajith had another daughter named Kushani from his first marriage to Sumana.

Ajith Silva died intestate on 2 March 2019, and Prabash Silva died intestate on 2 June 2019.

Prabash had two daughters, namely Sunali and Bimali, by his first wife Sheela, and two sons, namely Brian and Rian, by his second wife Linda. Sheela died intestate on 5 August 2019. Brian married Sara and thereafter died in an accident on 25 September 2021 without having children. Sunali died on 10 October 2023 unmarried and issueless.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Ajith Silva up to the present owners in relation to the property bearing Assessment No. 12, Temple Road, Nugegoda. **(20 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(5 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

By a Final Decree dated 5 May 2018, entered in partition case bearing No. 3535/P of the District Court of Nugegoda, Ajith Silva was allotted all that allotment of land marked Lot 2 depicted in Plan No. 1616 dated 2 March 2010, made by A. C. Perera, Licensed Surveyor, of the land called Kahatagahawatte, bearing Assessment No. 12, Temple Road, Nugegoda, containing in extent 15 perches.

Ajith Silva, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 December 2018, attested by P. C. Nonis, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot 2 depicted in Plan No. 1616 to Prabash Silva, the elder son of Ajith, subject to the life interest of the donor, and subject to the condition that Prabash shall not sell, mortgage or otherwise deal with the land, but may enjoy the produce thereof during his lifetime. On the death of Prabash, the property shall devolve free of all conditions to Subash, the younger son of Ajith Silva.

Ajith had three children, namely Prabash, Subash and Shehani, by his second marriage to Yamuna. Ajith had another daughter named Kushani from his first marriage to Sumana.

Ajith Silva died intestate on 2 March 2019, and Prabash Silva died intestate on 2 June 2019.

Prabash had two daughters, namely Sunali and Bimali, by his first wife Sheela, and two sons, namely Brian and Rian, by his second wife Linda. Sheela died intestate on 5 August 2019. Brian married Sara and thereafter died in an accident on 25 September 2021 without having children. Sunali died on 10 October 2023 unmarried and issueless.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Ajith Silva up to the present owners in relation to the property bearing Assessment No. 12, Temple Road, Nugegoda. **(20 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(5 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

claims.text: Under section 44 of the Registration of Title Act, a Notary Public attesting an instrument must: (a) satisfy himself of the identity of unknown parties and witnesses using official identity cards or other reliable means; (b) satisfy himself of the capacity of the parties by referring to the Title Registry records or an extract from the relevant Title Register; and (c) satisfy himself of the identity of the land and state of the title by reference to the Certificate of Title and Title Registry records.

For initial compilation, the Commissioner of Title Settlement must: first, on publication of an Order under section 1, request the Surveyor-General to prepare cadastral maps for the specified areas; second, upon receiving certified copies of the maps, publish a Notice in the Gazette calling for claimants to submit their claims within a prescribed period; and third, if subsequent findings require it, request the Surveyor-General to conduct additional surveys to reflect those findings on the cadastral map.

claims.text: Under the Notaries Ordinance, as amended, a notary must not execute or attest: (1) any deed or instrument written on ola; (2) any deed or instrument written on paper that is not of a reasonably durable description; (3) any deed or instrument written on more than one entire or undivided parchment paper or blue sheet unless either each sheet is pre-marked/signed/initialled by the Registrar of Lands of the notary's district, or both the executing parties and the notary sign every sheet and the pages are numbered; and (4) he must not sign his name or make his mark upon any paper intended for his protocol or a draft/copy until the entire deed or instrument has been written or engrossed thereon.

To obtain the annual certificate to practice, a notary must deliver: (1) a written declaration signed by him stating his name, place(s) of residence, the exact situation of his office(s), and the judicial zone of practice; and (2) an annexed affidavit stating that he forwarded all duplicates of deeds/instruments attested by him in the previous year to the Registrar of Lands and that any money imposed by the Registrar-General under section 35 has been paid. The exact deadline date for this submission is not specified in the retrieved text.
A notary must affix passport-size photographs of the signatories (excluding witnesses) to the protocol for a deed of transfer, a deed of gift, a deed of exchange, or a will.
